In \(\square\)IJKL, side IJ \(\parallel\) side KL.
Side JK is a transversal, so \(\angle J\) and \(\angle K\) are interior angles on the same side of it and are supplementary.
So \(\angle J = 180^{\circ} - 53^{\circ} = 127^{\circ}\).
Side LI is a transversal, so \(\angle I\) and \(\angle L\) are supplementary.
So \(\angle L = 180^{\circ} - 108^{\circ} = 72^{\circ}\).
Hence \(\angle J = 127^{\circ}\) and \(\angle L = 72^{\circ}\).

In \(\square\)ABCD, side BC \(\parallel\) side AD and side AB \(\cong\) side DC, so it is an isosceles trapezium with AD and BC as the parallel sides.
Side AB is a transversal of the parallel sides, so \(\angle A\) and \(\angle B\) are interior angles on the same side and are supplementary.
So \(\angle B = 180^{\circ} - 72^{\circ} = 108^{\circ}\).
The non-parallel sides AB and DC are congruent, so the angles at the ends of side AD are congruent, that is \(\angle D = \angle A\).
So \(\angle D = 72^{\circ}\).
Hence \(\angle B = 108^{\circ}\) and \(\angle D = 72^{\circ}\).

Construction: through C draw seg CE \(\parallel\) seg BA, meeting side AD at point E. Since side BC \(<\) side AD, the point E lies between A and D.
In \(\square\)ABCE, side BC \(\parallel\) side AE (given, as E is on side AD) and side BA \(\parallel\) side CE (construction), so \(\square\)ABCE is a parallelogram.
So \(CE = BA\) (opposite sides of a parallelogram).
Given side BA \(\cong\) side CD, so \(CE = CD\) and \(\triangle\)CED is isosceles.
So \(\angle CED \cong \angle CDE\) (angles opposite congruent sides).
Seg CE \(\parallel\) seg BA with transversal AD, so \(\angle CED \cong \angle BAD\) (corresponding angles).
So \(\angle BAD \cong \angle CDA\).
Now side BC \(\parallel\) side AD, so with transversal AB, \(\angle ABC + \angle BAD = 180^{\circ}\), and with transversal CD, \(\angle DCB + \angle CDA = 180^{\circ}\).
Since \(\angle BAD = \angle CDA\), it follows that \(\angle ABC = \angle DCB\).
Hence \(\angle ABC \cong \angle DCB\).
